resolutions.researcher_notes: Old ref (egyptoil-gas 'Western Desert' report) is dead/content-stripped (page loads 200 but article body has been removed, replaced with only nav/footer boilerplate; no 'Qasr' or 'Shams' text present). Two independent working sources confirm an active, in-service Qasr-to-Shams export gas line as part of Khalda Petroleum Co. (KPC, Apache/EGPC JV)'s Western Desert gathering system: (1) target-engineering.com contractor case study 'KPC Qasr - Installation' describing the built and commissioned SCADA/PCS system controlling 'the pipeline to Shams' from the Qasr Manifold (present-tense operational description, includes plant-expansion narrative showing continued operation); (2) Daily News Egypt (2016-11-21), quoting Khalda's head, describing ongoing 'gas pumping...from the Qasr area...in an 18-inch line, to Shams area, then to Al-Abyad' -- i.e. actively flowing gas. Also corroborated (third, non-independent-enough-alone but consistent) by Egypt Oil & Gas 2017 feature on the Qasr Gas Compression Project, which describes gas 'currently free flow[ing]... through the export pipelines... to the SHAMS manifold and the Salam gas plant.' All three describe the line as in active service through at least 2017; no source suggests it has been shut in. Status=operating supported at high confidence.

Could not verify GEM's stated capacity of 350 MMcf/d for this specific Qasr-Shams segment from any independent source; old ref (egyptoil-gas Western Desert report) is dead/content-stripped and never actually names a 350 MMcf/d figure even in its indexed form. CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: Daily News Egypt (2016-11-21, quoting Khalda's head, verified working -- https://dailynewsegypt.com/2016/11/21/apache-allocates-909m-drilling-97-wells-fy-20162017-khalda-petroleum-head/) states the Qasr-to-Shams-to-Al-Abyad line runs 'at a capacity of 250m cubic gas per day' (i.e. ~250 MMcf/d), not 350. Other sources cite adjacent-but-different capacity figures for the broader Qasr/Salam system (670 MMcfd field production per Egypt Oil & Gas 2020 Western Desert report search snippet; 800 MMcfd Qasr field peak rate and 600 MMcfd Salam plant capacity per Egypt Oil & Gas 2017 KPC Gas Compression Project feature; 510 MMcfd Khalda plant capacity per OGJ), none of which match 350 MMcf/d either, and none specific to the Qasr-Shams pipe segment itself. Leaving Capacity value/ref UNRESOLVED rather than fabricating a match; recommend a human check whether 350 MMcf/d is a stale/superseded design capacity or a transcription of a different line, given the 250 MMcf/d figure found for this exact segment.

Route (Qasr -> Shams, Egypt) confirmed at high confidence by 2 independent working sources: target-engineering.com's KPC Qasr Installation case study ('the pipeline to Shams' from 'Qasr Manifold') and Daily News Egypt (2016-11-21: gas pumped 'from the Qasr area...in an 18-inch line, to Shams area'). StartCountryOrArea/EndCountryOrArea=Egypt trivially confirmed by both. StartState/Province=EndState/Province=Matruh is only circumstantially supported, not explicitly named by any source found: an open-access geology paper (medcraveonline.com, verified working) places the Qasr field at approx. 30.36-30.39N/26.41-26.44E [note: source states 30 36'-30 39'N, 26 41'-26 44'E], 'west of Qattara Depression' in the Western Desert -- coordinates that fall within Matruh Governorate's normal southward extent (which runs from the Mediterranean coast down past Siwa), and Daily News Egypt separately confirms Khalda's Western Desert CSR activity is centered on 'Matrouh' governorate/residents -- but no single source directly labels the Qasr or Shams sites as being IN Matruh Governorate by name. Downgraded to tier=medium and flagged for a human check on the Matruh province attribution specifically, even though the Qasr/Shams route itself is solid. Diameter note (out of scope for this unit but worth flagging): Daily News Egypt states an 18-inch line, vs. GEM's stated 24 in -- a discrepancy for a human to review alongside the Capacity conflict above.
